svg.title: How the code is laid out
svg.desc: Every line that ships is TypeScript in src/, built into extension/lib/; extension/ holds only the manifest, the HTML, the styles, the icons and the texts. The popup and the switcher are pages of the extension that pages/players.ts draws, the options page keeps the settings of the button and of the venue mode, and the welcome page guides the first set-up; what they decide is in popup-model.ts and options-model.ts. They send their requests, typed in messages.ts, to worker.ts, the service worker, which background.ts starts on the real chrome and which wires the browser to the logic. There switch.ts makes every change of the accounts, one at a time through queue.ts, with state.ts for the saved accounts, storage.ts to store them with the version of their format, vault.ts to seal their sessions and passwords, and autodarts.ts for the sign-in service of Autodarts; tabs.ts picks the Autodarts tab, health.ts plans the renewal and the badge, page.ts decides for the switcher, onboarding.ts for the first set-up and the bug report, trust.ts who may send which request and who may read the storage, and venue.ts the PINs and the return after a break of the venue mode. The worker reaches chrome.storage.local, the IndexedDB of the key, api.autodarts.com and the content script only through ChromeApi, the typed port that background.ts fills with the real chrome and a test with a fake one. content.ts runs in each Autodarts tab as a classic script, shows the button and the frame of the switcher, and is the only code that reads or writes the session of the page.
